draft.title: Types of data
card: data sorted into groups or labels. Nominal data has no natural order, such as eye colour. Ordinal data has a natural order, such as shirt size (small, medium, large).
data that is a count or a measurement. Discrete data is counted and takes separate values, such as the number of pets. Continuous data is measured and can take any value in a range, such as height.
A quick test: if you can do sensible arithmetic with the values, the data is numerical. Postcodes are numbers, but adding them means nothing, so they are categorical.
Categorical data suits a bar chart or segmented bar chart. Numerical data suits a histogram or dot plot. A histogram is best for continuous data.
draft.remember: Categories name groups. Numbers count or measure. Work out the type before you choose a display.

a.q: Each student in a Year 11 class counts how many siblings they have. What type of data is this?
a.why: Siblings are counted, so the data is numerical and takes separate values: discrete. It is not continuous, because nobody has 1.5 siblings.

b.q: A café in Ballarat asks customers to rate its service as poor, fair, good or excellent. What type of data is this, and which display suits it?
b.why: The ratings are labels with a natural order, so the data is categorical and ordinal. Categorical data suits a bar chart. Nominal is wrong because the order of the ratings matters.
b.clue: Could you do sensible arithmetic with these ratings?

proposal.title: Types of data
card: data sorted into groups or labels. Nominal data has no natural order, such as eye colour. Ordinal data has a natural order, such as shirt size (small, medium, large).
data that is a count or a measurement. Discrete data is counted and takes separate values, such as the number of pets. Continuous data is measured and can take any value in a range, such as height.
A quick test: if you can do sensible arithmetic with the values, the data is numerical. Postcodes are numbers, but adding them means nothing, so they are categorical.
Measured data stays continuous even when it is rounded. A height written as 172 cm has been rounded, but the true height could be any value close to it.
proposal.remember: Categorical data names groups. Numerical data counts or measures. Ask: counted, measured, or just a label?

a.q: Each student in a Year 11 class counts how many siblings they have. What type of data is this?
a.why: Siblings are counted, so the data is numerical and takes separate values: discrete. It is not continuous, because nobody has 1.5 siblings.

b.q: A coach in Bendigo times each runner over 100 m, rounding each time to the nearest tenth of a second. What type of data is this?
b.why: Time is measured, so the data is numerical and continuous. Rounding to a tenth of a second makes the values look separate, but a runner's true time could be any value in a range, so it is not discrete.
b.clue: Does rounding change how the time was found?
